name: ALCOSAN Sewer Overflow Advisory Key (SOAK) online overflow log
waters_covered: System-wide advisory for the Allegheny, Monongahela and Ohio rivers in the ALCOSAN service area (Allegheny County); no per-outfall detail
access_detail: Server-rendered HTML (Sitefinity). Five log entries per page; older pages at /clean-water-plan/sewer-overflow-advisories/{n} (n=2..). Pages 1-32 fetched 2026-11-02: 160 entries back to 2025-07-08; deeper pages continue. No JSON/RSS. Annual PDFs (Everbridge export with Notification ID) for 2014-2025 plus a 1995-2013 summary under /docs/default-source/cso-advisories/. Old URL /our-plan/sewer-overflow-advisories redirects.

sample_record.status: Overflows have ceased; Waterways may still be impaired.

cadence: Status posted 8 a.m.-7 p.m. daily, April 1-October 31; changes outside those hours posted at 8 a.m. next day. Hand-typed times: typos seen (e.g. '07:33 AN', '06/22/2016', '08/17:2025', '08/20/205', '9/3/26 - 6:30' without AM/PM, '06/18/2026' for 07/18).
history: HTML pagination reaches back through 2025 at least; PDFs 2014-2025; summary 1995-2013.
license: No data licence or terms statement found on the page.
legal_basis: ALCOSAN NPDES permit PA0025984 / 2008 consent decree; CSO Nine Minimum Controls public notification (EPA CSO Control Policy 1994). Not a state statute.
status_reason: Best PA event record: real start/end times for every overflow period, three-stage wording, season-long history. HTML scrape only; one system-wide status, not per outfall.
notes: Advisory wording ties to 'orange CSO flags' at nine sites. Allegheny County Health Department gives a different post-event window. ALCOSAN signs at 259 CSO and 53 SSO structures; dry-weather hotline 888-936-9363.

name: ALCOSAN SOAK text/email alerts (Everbridge)
access_detail: Everbridge member portal sign-up (text and email). Not subscribed (brief rule). The 2025 annual PDF is an Everbridge export: Notification ID, Incident Template ('Overflows in Effect', 'Overflows Ceased', 'Dry Weather Operation'), Message Body.
cadence: Push at each status change, 8 a.m.-7 p.m.; overnight changes at 8 a.m.
status_reason: Owner should subscribe: email timestamps give reported_at, which the web log lacks.
notes: Sign-up URL fetched from the ALCOSAN page; not opened.

name: ALCOSAN CSO Flag Alert Program (nine orange flag sites)
waters_covered: Nine riverfront sites on the Allegheny, Monongahela and Ohio
access_detail: Physical flags; site list on SOAK page and a 2022 PDF map. Sites: James Sharp Landing (Sharpsburg), Three Rivers Rowing Association, Washington's Landing 2 and 3, Redfin Blues (Allegheny); Braddock Boat Ramp, Southside Riverfront Park (Monongahela); Carnegie Science Center, Peggy's Harbor Marina (Ohio).
status_reason: Use the nine flag sites as named advisory points on the three river pages; the state comes from the SOAK log.

name: Philadelphia Water Department CSOcast (Combined Sewer Overflow Public Notification System)
waters_covered: 164 CSO outfalls: Delaware River (D, 53), Schuylkill River (S, 40), Cobbs Creek (C, 34), Frankford Creek (F, 17), Tacony Creek (T, 15), Pennypack Creek (P, 5)
access_detail: Public ArcGIS Online FeatureServer (owner phillywatergis, item 70e9d70fd2674f8896e0b560f88040b2, capabilities Query): https://services2.arcgis.com/POWz8dBwmjnei8fu/ArcGIS/rest/services/CSOCast_Layerboard/FeatureServer/0 (ows_csocast_outfall_status, 164 points) and /1 (ows_csocast_raingauge_status). No auth. Fetched all 164 rows 2026-11-02 17:55 UTC.

sample_record.Name: C_01
sample_record.Status_Message: No overflow in the past 72 hours.
sample_record.Street: City Line Ave and Haveford Ave

cadence: Polled per outfall roughly every few minutes to hours; layer lastEditDate 2026-11-02 17:50 UTC at fetch. LastPoll epoch equals the local wall-clock LastPoll_DATE/TIME, so the epoch is Eastern local time labelled as UTC (inferred from edit time).
history: None: a current-state layer. Building history means polling and storing state changes ourselves.
license: No licence on the item (licenseInfo null). Map text: 'CSOcast is not intended to be used as a water quality notification system for recreation.'
legal_basis: PWD NPDES permits PA0026689, PA0026662, PA0026671 (CSO public notification under Nine Minimum Controls) and the 2011 Green City, Clean Waters Consent Order and Agreement with PA DEP.
status_reason: The only per-outfall, machine-readable CSO status feed in PA. At fetch 64 of 164 outfalls read 'Data is not currently available.' and 13 had LastPoll dates months or years old; no outfall was overflowing.
notes: Domain values say '24 hours' but rows say 'No overflow in the past 72 hours.'. Page text: 'Waterways where a combined sewer outfall is overflowing are unsafe for any type of recreation, and may remain unsafe for recreation for a period of up to 72 hours following storm events, particularly in the Delaware and tidal Schuylkill rivers.' Disclaimer calls CSOcast 'a pilot program' using flow monitors and a SWMM model. No email/text sign-up on the map.

access_detail: Fields Name, Message, LastPoll, Latitude, Longitude, rainfall_vol_in, LastPoll_DATE, LastPoll_TIME. Message domain: 'No rain reported in the last 48 hours for this area.' / 'Rain reported in the last 48 hours for this area.'

status_reason: Second-best PA event feed after ALCOSAN: per-outfall start/end/volume, date-range queries, coordinates. Unit of 'Discharge (Gallons)' needs confirming (values like 0.05886 and 306.1 suggest millions of gallons).

name: PA DEP Combined Sewer Overflows FAQ (Dec 14, 2020, v1.0)
access_detail: Wayback copy 2025-09-03 read (20 pp.).
status_reason: DEP's own statement of what CSO notification means in PA.
notes: FAQ #34: 'All CSO permittees should have as part of their NMCs a public notification plan to inform the public of when a CSO discharge has occurred and potential impacts. The timing and method of public notice may [vary - word lost in extraction]... Residents can ask their local municipality or sewer authority for a copy of the notification plan'. FAQ #33: 'Locations of CSO outfalls should be identified along surface waters through signage.' FAQ #35: 'DEP recommends that recreational activities be avoided immediately downstream of CSO outfalls'. NMC 8 examples: 'Posting (at outfalls, use areas, public places) TV/newspaper notification Direct mail notification'.

name: 25 Pa. Code § 91.33 Incidents causing or threatening pollution
access_detail: Fetched (Code current through 56 Pa.B. 5370, Aug 8, 2026).
legal_basis: (a) '...it is the responsibility of the person ... to immediately notify the Department by telephone of the location and nature of the danger and, if reasonably possible to do so, to notify known downstream users of the waters.'
status_reason: The only general notice duty: to DEP and, 'if reasonably possible', known downstream users. No duty to notify the public.

name: 25 Pa. Code § 92a.41(b) NPDES conditions: 4-hour oral notice, 5-day written
legal_basis: 'Oral notification is required as soon as possible, but no later than 4 hours after the permittee becomes aware of the incident causing or threatening pollution. A written submission shall also be provided within 5 days ... The written submission must conform to the requirements of 40 CFR 122.41(l)(6).'
status_reason: Sets the deadline for telling DEP (not the public).

name: 25 Pa. Code § 92a.47(b)-(c) CSO NMC/LTCP duty; SSOs prohibited
legal_basis: (b) 'Dischargers of sewage from a CSO shall implement, as approved by the Department, nine minimum controls (NMCs) and a long-term control plan (LTCP)...' (c) 'Discharges from an SSO are prohibited.'
status_reason: The hook for public notification (NMC 8) is indirect, through the NMCs; no timing or channel set in regulation.

name: 25 Pa. Code § 94.12 Chapter 94 annual wasteload management report
legal_basis: Report due 'by March 31 of each year to the appropriate regional office'; must discuss sewer condition to 'prevent or eliminate bypassing, combined sewer overflow, sanitary sewer overflow'.
status_reason: Annual reports go to DEP regional offices; not published online as a dataset (file review). Context only.

name: Standard PA NPDES CSO permit conditions (example: Scranton PA0026492, 2012 final permit)
access_detail: Live host unreachable; read the Wayback copy (2017-05-02). A 2025-08-04 draft renewal exists (PA0026492_NPDES_PERMIT_20250804_DRAFT_V3.pdf) but is not archived.
legal_basis: Part A III.C.4.a: oral notice to DEP 'no later than 4 hours'; '(ii) If reasonably possible to do so, the permittee shall immediately notify downstream users ... Such notice shall include the location and nature of the danger.' Part C CSO: NMC 8 'Public notification to ensure that the public receives adequate notification of CSO occurrences and CSO impacts.' Supplemental DMR for CSOs: for monitored regulators report 'location, date, time, and duration of wet weather overflows'; dry-weather CSOs prohibited, immediate phone notice to DEP.
status_reason: Permit text is where PA's CSO notice duty lives; it names no deadline or channel for the public. Per-overflow records go to DEP on supplemental DMRs, which are not online.
